# AWS Provider

Use the Amazon Web Services (AWS) provider to interact with the
many resources supported by AWS. You must configure the provider
with the proper credentials before you can use it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

resource "aws_vpc" "example" {
  cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"
}
```

## Authentication and Configuration

Configuration for the AWS Provider can be derived from several sources, applied in the following order:

1. Parameters in the provider configuration
1. Environment variables
1. Shared credentials files
1. Shared configuration files
1. Container credentials
1. Instance profile credentials and Region

## Argument Reference

* `region` - (Optional) AWS Region where the provider will operate. Can also be set with the `AWS_REGION` environment variable.
* `profile` - (Optional) AWS profile name as set in the shared configuration and credentials files.
* `assume_role` - (Optional) Configuration block for an assumed role.
* `default_tags` - (Optional) Configuration block with resource tag settings to apply across all resources handled by this provider.

provider_docs.content:

subcategory: "EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)"

---

# Resource: aws_instance

Provides an EC2 instance resource. This allows instances to be created, updated, and deleted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "aws_ami" "ubuntu" {
  most_recent = true

  filter {
    name   = "name"
    values = ["ubuntu/images/hvm-ssd/ubuntu-jammy-22.04-amd64-server-*"]
  }

  owners = ["099720109477"] # Canonical
}

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
  instance_type = "t3.micro"

  tags = {
    Name = "HelloWorld"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `ami` - (Optional) AMI to use for the instance.
* `instance_type` - (Optional) Instance type to use for the instance.
* `subnet_id` - (Optional) VPC Subnet ID to launch in.
* `vpc_security_group_ids` - (Optional) List of security group IDs to associate with.
* `tags` - (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the resource.

## Attribute Reference

* `arn` - ARN of the instance.
* `id` - ID of the instance.
* `private_ip` - Private IP address assigned to the instance.
* `public_ip` - Public IP address assigned to the instance, if applicable.

# Resource: aws_s3_bucket

Provides a S3 bucket resource.

-> This functionality is for managing S3 in an AWS Partition. To manage S3 on Outposts, see the `aws_s3control_bucket` resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "example" {
  bucket = "my-tf-test-bucket"

  tags = {
    Name        = "My bucket"
    Environment = "Dev"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `bucket` - (Optional, Forces new resource) Name of the bucket. If omitted, Terraform will assign a random, unique name.
* `force_destroy` - (Optional, Default:`false`) Boolean that indicates all objects should be deleted from the bucket when the bucket is destroyed.
* `object_lock_enabled` - (Optional, Forces new resource) Indicates whether this bucket has an Object Lock configuration enabled.
* `tags` - (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the bucket.

## Attribute Reference

* `arn` - ARN of the bucket.
* `bucket_domain_name` - Bucket domain name.
* `region` - AWS region this bucket resides in.

provider_docs.title: aws_db_instance
provider_docs.content:
---
subcategory: "RDS (Relational Database)"
layout: "aws"
page_title: "AWS: aws_db_instance"
description: |-
  Provides an RDS instance resource. A DB instance is an isolated database environment in the cloud. A DB instance can contain multiple user-created databases.
---

# Resource: aws_db_instance

Provides an RDS instance resource.

~> **Note:** All arguments including the username and password will be stored in the raw state as plain-text.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aws_db_instance" "default" {
  allocated_storage    = 10
  db_name              = "mydb"
  engine               = "postgres"
  engine_version       = "16.4"
  instance_class       = "db.t3.micro"
  username             = "foo"
  manage_master_user_password = true
  skip_final_snapshot  = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `allocated_storage` - (Required unless a `snapshot_identifier` or `replicate_source_db` is provided) The allocated storage in gibibytes.
* `allow_major_version_upgrade` - (Optional) Indicates that major version upgrades are allowed. Changing this parameter does not result in an outage and the change is asynchronously applied as soon as possible.
* `engine` - (Required unless a `snapshot_identifier` or `replicate_source_db` is provided) The database engine to use.
* `engine_version` - (Optional) The engine version to use. If `auto_minor_version_upgrade` is enabled, you can provide a prefix of the version such as `16` (for `16.4`).
* `instance_class` - (Required) The instance type of the RDS instance.
* `multi_az` - (Optional) Specifies if the RDS instance is multi-AZ.

## Attribute Reference

* `address` - The hostname of the RDS instance.
* `endpoint` - The connection endpoint in `address:port` format.

Provides a VPC resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aws_vpc" "main" {
  cidr_block       = "10.0.0.0/16"
  instance_tenancy = "default"

  tags = {
    Name = "main"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `cidr_block` - (Optional) The IPv4 CIDR block for the VPC.
* `enable_dns_hostnames` - (Optional) A boolean flag to enable/disable DNS hostnames in the VPC. Defaults false.
* `enable_dns_support` - (Optional) A boolean flag to enable/disable DNS support in the VPC. Defaults to true.

## Attribute Reference

* `arn` - Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of VPC
* `id` - The ID of the VPC

provider_docs.content:

description: |-
  Provides a resource to create a VPC NAT Gateway.
---

# Resource: aws_nat_gateway

Provides a resource to create a VPC NAT Gateway.

## Example Usage

### Public NAT

```terraform
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "example" {
  allocation_id = aws_eip.example.id
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.example.id

  tags = {
    Name = "gw NAT"
  }

  depends_on = [aws_internet_gateway.example]
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `allocation_id` - (Optional) The Allocation ID of the Elastic IP address for the NAT Gateway. Required for `connectivity_type` of `public`.
* `connectivity_type` - (Optional) Connectivity type for the NAT Gateway. Valid values are `private` and `public`. Defaults to `public`.
* `subnet_id` - (Required) The Subnet ID of the subnet in which to place the NAT Gateway.

## Attribute Reference

* `id` - The ID of the NAT Gateway.
* `public_ip` - The Elastic IP address associated with the NAT Gateway.

provider_docs.content:

subcategory: "ECS (Elastic Container)"
layout: "aws"
page_title: "AWS: aws_ecs_service"
description: |-
  Provides an ECS service.
---

# Resource: aws_ecs_service

Provides an ECS service - effectively a task that is expected to run until an error occurs or a user terminates it (typically a webserver or a database).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aws_ecs_service" "mongo" {
  name            = "mongodb"
  cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.foo.id
  task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.mongo.arn
  desired_count   = 3
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `name` - (Required) Name of the service (up to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores)
* `desired_count` - (Optional) Number of instances of the task definition to place and keep running. Defaults to 0.
* `launch_type` - (Optional) Launch type on which to run your service. The valid values are `EC2`, `FARGATE`, and `EXTERNAL`.

# Data Source: aws_ami

Use this data source to get the ID of a registered AMI for use in other resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "aws_ami" "example" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["self"]

  filter {
    name   = "name"
    values = ["myami-*"]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `owners` - (Optional) List of AMI owners to limit search.
* `most_recent` - (Optional) If more than one result is returned, use the most recent AMI.
* `filter` - (Optional) One or more name/value pairs to filter off of.

# Terraform AWS Provider Version 5 Upgrade Guide

Version 5.0.0 of the AWS provider for Terraform is a major release and includes changes that you need to consider when upgrading.

## Provider Version Configuration

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
}
```

## Provider Arguments

Version 5.0.0 removes these `provider` arguments: `assume_role.duration_seconds`, `s3_force_path_style`, `shared_credentials_file`, `skip_get_ec2_platforms`.

## Default Tags

The following enhancements are included: duplicate `default_tags` can now be included and will be overwritten by resource `tags`.

# Function: arn_parse

Parses an ARN into its constituent parts.

See the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference-arns.html) for additional information on Amazon Resource Names.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# result:
# {
#   "partition": "aws",
#   "service": "iam",
#   "region": "",
#   "account_id": "444455556666",
#   "resource": "role/example",
# }
output "example" {
  value = provider::aws::arn_parse("arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/example")
}
```

## Signature

```text
arn_parse(arn string) object
```

subcategory: "Compute Engine"

---

# google_compute_instance

Manages a VM instance resource within GCE.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "google_compute_instance" "default" {
  name         = "my-instance"
  machine_type = "n2-standard-2"
  zone         = "us-central1-a"

  boot_disk {
    initialize_params {
      image = "debian-cloud/debian-12"
    }
  }

  network_interface {
    network = "default"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

* `boot_disk` - (Required) The boot disk for the instance.
* `machine_type` - (Required) The machine type to create.
* `name` - (Required) A unique name for the resource.
* `zone` - (Optional) The zone that the machine should be created in.

```terraform
resource "google_sql_database_instance" "main" {
  name             = "main-instance"

  region           = "us-central1"

Identical to `random_string` with the exception that the result is treated as sensitive and, thus, _not_ displayed in console output.

}
```

root.readme:
# AWS VPC Terraform module

Terraform module which creates VPC resources on AWS.

## Usage

```hcl
module "vpc" {
  source = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws"

  name = "my-vpc"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"

  azs             = ["eu-west-1a", "eu-west-1b", "eu-west-1c"]
  private_subnets = ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"]
  public_subnets  = ["10.0.101.0/24", "10.0.102.0/24", "10.0.103.0/24"]

  enable_nat_gateway = true
  enable_vpn_gateway = true
}
```

inputs.description: Should be true to enable DNS hostnames in the VPC

latest-version.readme:
# Pre-written Sentinel Policies for AWS CIS Foundations Benchmarking

The Center for Internet Security (CIS) AWS Foundations Benchmark provides prescriptive guidance for configuring security options for a subset of Amazon Web Services.

## Policies included

- Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22
- Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389
- Ensure the default security group of every VPC restricts all traffic
- Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs

## Usage

Add the policies to a `sentinel.hcl` file in your policy set repository.

policies.title: EC2 security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22

policies.name: ec2-security-group-ingress-traffic-restriction-port-3389
policies.title: EC2 security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389

policies.name: ec2-vpc-default-security-group-no-traffic
policies.title: The default security group of every VPC should restrict all traffic

policies.name: ec2-vpc-flow-logging-enabled
policies.title: VPC flow logging should be enabled in all VPCs

# Pre-written Sentinel Policies for AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

This policy set enforces the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard, a set of controls that detect when your AWS accounts and resources deviate from security best practices.

## Policies included

- S3 general purpose buckets should block public access
- RDS DB instances should have encryption at-rest enabled
- EBS default encryption should be enabled
